description:
Return the build kit for one design system. Pass `designSystemId` from `find-design-system`, or the `projectId` of a generated system. Reuse the system already selected: a redesign does not authorize changing it or its assigned icons.

Pick the target by what the host can do, not by habit:
- `target: "react"`: the host can write files and run a terminal (Claude Code, Cursor, an IDE agent, Claude Desktop with filesystem and shell tools, any checked-out repo). Returns ONE shadcn command that installs every component into components/ui/. Run it before writing feature code, then build real React components. A standalone .html file as "the app" is a bug when you could run the install.
- `target: "html"`: a pure inline chat canvas or artifact with no file writes and no terminal (ChatGPT canvas, a Claude.ai chat artifact). Returns the framework-free token and component CSS kit. Its class contract is mandatory: paste the kit CSS verbatim, keep `class="ds"` on the artifact root, keep the `ds-*` component classes on interactive controls, and never rename or replace the `ds-*` classes. Custom classes are for layout only.
- `target: "react-native"` for a React Native or Expo app and `target: "swiftui"` for an iOS app, never the react target. Each returns this system's theme and native components for that platform, plus the handoff to the matching guide.
- `target: "shopify"`: the user is styling a Shopify store or theme. Returns Liquid theme files to write, plus the mandatory handoff to `get-shopify-guide`.
The `target` input lists the other targets.

React only: Base UI (@base-ui/react) is the default flavor. BEFORE installing, check the project: if package.json has any @radix-ui/* dependency, pass `library: "radix"`. Keep every dependency version the project already has; if the install would change one, report that conflict and stop. Pass `component` only when the user asks to inspect or customise a specific component's source.

Build only the screens the user asked for, from the system's own components and tokens. Hierarchy is pass-fail: give the first view one main task and at most one summary, and move history, detail and empty-state chrome below it or behind a tab. A dashboard starts with its page title, one supporting line and one primary action. Most replies carry these and the other build rules in full: follow them. For a pitch deck or presentation in a coding host, use Open Slide (`@open-slide/core`) and call this tool with `target: "open-slide"` for its theme and layouts. After writing the UI, call `get-review-rules`.

Classify the request as repair, polish or redesign, and follow the user's scope: do not turn a redesign into polish, widen a repair, or turn a token export into a redesign. Keep the selected design system and its assigned icons unless the user asks to change them. Preserve unrelated behavior, accessibility, production and control pages, and every paragraph, review, offer detail, link and disclosure the user supplied, unless the user asks to cut or rewrite it. Before choosing or changing a design direction, tell the user in the conversation what each real option gains and loses, which users or team bear the cost, and why it fits this project's known audience, goals, and constraints. Label assumptions. Do not invent research, metrics or project facts. If the user has already chosen, explain the trade-off without reopening the choice. This adds no approval step and never excuses an accessibility or safety failure. Before presenting the result, check that you said this.

component.description: React only. The component or components whose source the user asked to inspect. Omit to install the whole system.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

designSystemId.description: Catalog design system ID from find-design-system. Pass this or projectId.

files.description: react-native only, when the server does not write the kit: the kit files to return, by path, file name or export name, such as ["button", "card"]. The reply adds every kit file they import, the theme and ThemeProvider. Leave it out first: the reply lists every component.

install.description: SwiftUI and React Native: leave this out. The server then writes the kit's theme and component files into the app folder, and for SwiftUI a ContentView.swift home screen when the folder has none. It never writes an App struct, an Xcode project or a package. Pass false only when the user said not to touch their files. React: true creates a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 project in an empty folder and installs the whole design system into it; it refuses an existing project, where you run the kit's install commands yourself.

library.description: React target only, default "base-ui". Pass "radix" when the project already uses Radix primitives.

projectDir.description: The absolute path of the project or app folder. Defaults to the folder this server runs in, which is the folder the user opened.

projectId.description: Generated project ID from create-design-system or get-design-system-status. Works with every target.

screen.description: react-native and swiftui only: a few words naming the screen you are building, such as "habit tracker today". The kit then shows how shipped apps built it.

target.description: Required build target. "react": any host with a filesystem and a terminal. "html": inline chat canvases and artifacts only. "shopify": Shopify stores and themes. "dtcg": a W3C Design Tokens document for Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, Terrazzo, or a Figma plugin that creates variables. "figma": the link of the Figma file a project was written into, or the Better Design plugin steps that make one. "store-screenshots": App Store and Google Play screenshots in this system, as slide files and a render script that writes PNG files at the store sizes. "open-slide": a pitch deck or presentation in this system, as an Open Slide theme, slide layouts and a starter deck. "react-native": a React Native or Expo app. "swiftui": an iOS app.

name: get-design-system-kit

buildInstructions.description: Required build, design-choice and review steps, for clients that read only structuredContent.

componentCss.description: HTML only. Paste this ds-* component stylesheet verbatim.

componentExampleHtml.description: HTML only. Starter markup with the .ds wrapper and ds-* classes.

compositionPolicy.description: HTML only. Layout density and container contract.

customCssScope.description: HTML and Shopify. Custom classes arrange layout only.

deckFiles.description: Open Slide only. Write each file verbatim at its path in the Open Slide workspace, then follow buildInstructions.

figmaFileUrl.description: Figma only. The Figma file this project was written into. Absent when none exists; buildInstructions then says how to make one.

hostIsolationCssTemplate.description: HTML only. Replace APP_ROOT with the root selector and paste after host/base CSS.

hoverPolicy.description: HTML and Shopify. Hover contract to verify before presenting.

iconInstructions.description: How to look up the selected icons, or a missing-selection warning.

iconLibrary.description: The system's icon family and variant. Reuse it; do not select another pack.

iconMaterialStatus.description: Shopify glyph metadata: current, or legacy and unverified. Not rendered review evidence.

iconSelectionStatus.description: Selected means the identity is known, not that rendered icons were reviewed.

installLibrary.description: The component library flavor installCommand installs.

installedTo.description: The project folder this server installed into. Build there; run no setup command.

localInstall.description: True when this server can install on the user's machine: call get-design-system-kit again with install: true.

minimumTextContrast.description: HTML and Shopify. Minimum contrast of visible text against its computed background.

nativeFiles.description: React Native and SwiftUI only. Write each file verbatim at its path.

newProjectCommand.description: Creates a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 project when there is none. Run it, then run installCommand inside the new my-app folder.

previewUrl.description: Public showcase URL. Falls back to viewUrl.

requiredComponentClassPrefix.description: HTML and Shopify. Interactive components keep this class prefix; never rename it.

requiredWrapperClass.description: HTML and Shopify. The root must keep this class.

screenshotFiles.description: Store screenshots only. Write each file verbatim at its path, then follow buildInstructions.

spinner.description: The Motion spinner that fits this system. Use it for every loading spinner.

supportedInstallationScope.description: The Shopify kit is not page-scoped. Withhold installation for a page-only task until isolated files and styles exist.

textColorPolicy.description: HTML and Shopify. Text color contract: never mute text with surface tokens or opacity.

themeFiles.description: Shopify only. Theme files to write verbatim at each path.

tokenScaleNote.description: React, HTML and DTCG. Which spacing and type values the system declares, and which are Tailwind v4 defaults.

tokensCss.description: The system's tokens as CSS custom properties.

tokensJson.description: DTCG only. The tokens as a W3C Design Tokens document. Write it to tokens.json.

unsupportedTokens.description: React Native and SwiftUI only. Tokens with no native value: a calc(), a var(), or a relative oklch(). Set them by hand if the screen needs them. A dropped dark token shows its light value on a dark screen.

viewUrl.description: Owner-facing Better Design page. May require login.

title: Get a Design System Build Kit
